messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: paging oncall-alex @oncall-alex @sre-zoe — streaming endpoint /v1/stream (eu-west-1) p95/p99 breach detected. p95=1.8s, p99=18s over the last 5m. Error rate up 3x. Auto-escalation: paging eng-runtime.

oncall-alex: ack. I’m looking now — can someone paste the top-line grafana panels and recent proxy logs? I’ll start a zoom if we need a quick war room. :phone:

sre-zoe: grabbing metrics. Early sign: proxy write latencies spiking, connection write_timeouts increasing. Upstream service cpu/latency looks normal.

sre-zoe: paste: ```
proxy.stream_write_ms.p99: 18032
proxy.stream_write_ms.p95: 1780
proxy.connections.write_timeouts: +127 (5m)
upstream.v1_stream.latency.p99: 210ms
client.read_window_size.distribution: many at 1-4 bytes
```

eng-runtime-jamar: this smells like tiny-read clients causing TCP backpressure and proxy buffering. We’ve seen similar when many websockets/SSE clients poll slowly — proxy buffers and stalls output.

support-raj: Customer impact: two customers reported truncated streams and reconnect loops. Tickets: #CS-1987, #CS-1989. Both on EU region, started ~1768101000.

eng-platform-lina: quick mitigation proposal: enable evict-slow-clients flag on edge-proxies for eu-west-1, decrease streaming write batch size to reduce buffering, and bump proxy keepalive/timeouts to avoid long hung writes. Recommend also a temporary fallback to non-streaming chunked responses for VIP tenants.

oncall-alex: agree. @eng-runtime-jamar please roll the evict flag. @eng-platform-lina can you preflight the keepalive change? I’ll coordinate with support/customer success for comms.

eng-runtime-jamar: running toggle now (will log actions). ```
# enable evict-slow-clients in eu-west proxies
kubectl -n infra patch configmap/proxy-flags -p '{"data":{"evict_slow_clients":"true"}}'
# force reload proxies gradually
kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/edge-proxy-eu-west
```

incidents-bot: ACTION: featureflag.eviction (eu-west-1) enabled by eng-runtime-jamar at 1768101405. Rolling restarts started.

sre-zoe: after first batch of restarts: p95 -> 0.45s, p99 -> 0.92s (3m window). write_timeouts trending down. Still a small tail at ~1.5s for certain origin IP ranges.

eng-platform-lina: applied keepalive tuning to proxy: keepalive_idle=15s -> 8s, write_timeout=30s -> 10s for streaming routes. Also reduced server-side write buffer size for streaming route.

support-raj: letting affected customers know: CS drafts sent. Asking if we should proactively offer session replay/logs.

customer-success-maria: yes please attach short explanation and ETA for permanent fix. CS tickets updated.

oncall-alex: good stabilization. Next steps: eng-runtime to investigate client behavior (are we seeing a new SDK or gateway behavior?), eng-platform to add an alert on client read window distribution, SRE to run a replay test to reproduce. I’ll close the active page once p99 < 1s for 10m.

eng-runtime-jamar: noted — initial trace shows a spike of clients from a single ASN causing many 1-byte reads. Starting deeper RCA on SDK keep-alive logic and client-side backpressure. Dumping a sample conn log: ```
[1768101300] conn=0x7f3a client=10.12.54.213 read_bytes=3 write_bytes=1024 last_read_age=42s
[1768101301] conn=0x7f3b client=10.12.54.214 read_bytes=2 write_bytes=512 last_read_age=51s
```

sre-zoe: marking incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Creating follow-up ticket for postmortem: PM-1083 (RCA, mitigation plan, long-term alerting).

oncall-alex: handing off to eng-runtime/jamar for RCA. If everyone agrees, I’ll clear the pager in 10m after monitoring window. Great work triaging quickly. :clap:

incidents-bot: PAGE CLOSED: auto-page cleared at 1768101899 (p99 sustained < 0.95s for 8m). Follow-up: PM-1083 created, CS notified.
